Первый промышленный робот встал на конве: The first industrial robot joined a General Motors assembly line. Its motions were recorded in advance, and the parts always lie in the same places, so the robot needs nothing else.
Ганс Моравек заметил: считать и играть в: Hans Moravec noticed that computing and playing chess are easy for machines, while seeing, grasping and walking like a one-year-old are very hard.
Сергей Левин с коллегами обучили одну не: Sergey Levine and colleagues trained a single neural network to output motor commands straight from a camera image, with no hand-written modules. This approach is called end-to-end. The network in Lab 1 is modeled on this work.
Обучение по показу и общие данные: Learning from demos and shared data
ALOHA и ACT: робот учится сложным движен: ALOHA and ACT: a robot learns complex two-handed motions from 10 minutes of human demonstrations. Open X-Embodiment: 21 organizations pooled recordings of 22 robots into one dataset to train a general model on it.
VLA (vision-language-action) — модель, к: A VLA (vision-language-action) model takes a camera image and a command in words and outputs robot actions. The term was introduced in 2023 by the authors of RT-2 at Google DeepMind. π0 from Physical Intelligence is one such model. Besides laundry, it assembles boxes and clears the table; it was trained on 10,000+ hours of robot recordings.
Записи работы роботов собирают тысячами: Recordings of robots at work are collected by the thousands of hours: Generalist AI reports 270,000 hours. Ken Goldberg compares the data gap between robots and language models to a "100,000-year gap".

Each module can be tested separately — and each has to be designed by hand. The σ on the arrow is the estimation error: how unsure the module is about where the cup is.
Один «чёрный ящик» от пикселей до моторо: One "black box" from pixels to motors. The behavior is set by data, not by lines of code.

VLA — модель «зрение — язык — действие»:: A VLA is a vision-language-action model: from camera images and a request in words it outputs robot actions. The diagram shows a two-level VLA, as in Figure Helix, NVIDIA GR00T N1 and Gemini Robotics: the slow model thinks, the fast one moves. It is end-to-end cut by rate. There are also single-model VLAs, such as RT-2 and π0. The numbers on the arrows are how many times per second a block passes its result to the next one: 7–10 Hz is 7–10 times per second, 1 kHz is a thousand.

Чем гибрид на схеме отличается от правил: How does the hybrid in the diagram differ from rules?
Это end-to-end, к которому добавили прав: It is end-to-end with a safety rule added
Восприятие делает нейросеть, а остальные: Perception is done by a neural network, and the other modules with their inputs and outputs are the same as in rules
Модулей в нём нет, нейросеть сразу выдаё: It has no modules; the network outputs motor commands directly
Гибрид — тот же модульный стек, что у пр: The hybrid is the same modular stack as rules, except perception is done by a neural network: the part where rules stop working in the open world. Many real systems are built this way: object detectors and segmentation have long been neural, while the modules with clear inputs and outputs are designed by an engineer.

Тихие отказы из лаборатории 1 в масштабе: Silent failures from Lab 1 at product scale: a safety net of rules, quality evaluation, the road from 90% to 99.9%.
Начнём с ситуации, к которой готовы все: Let's start with a situation all three are ready for: daylight, a red cup, nothing in the way. The engineer wrote the rules for it; the operator recorded the demonstrations in it.
<b>Все трое справились.</b> Там, где сит:
All three made it. Where the situation is covered by rules and by data, both approaches work. Look at Ada's "thoughts". The rules show the cup pixels they found (blue cells), the estimate of its position and the planned path. End-to-end has four "points of interest" p1–p4 that the network picked on its own. Which of them is about the cup and which are about nothing, the network won't say.

The difference between the approaches appears when conditions go beyond the familiar. Let's start with the light.
Солнце село, на кухне включили тёплый св: The sun has set and warm light is on in the kitchen. Everything else is as before.
<b>Правила отказали, end-to-end и гибрид:
The rules failed, end-to-end and the hybrid made it. The engineer tuned the perception rule in daylight: "red channel above 0.60". Warm dim light dropped the cup's red channel to about 0.54, and the rule stopped firing. Switch the camera below to the "Rule" mode: no blue cells. The networks saw varied lighting in the demonstrations and learned a feature robust to it. Notice that the rules failed loudly: Ada knows she cannot see the cup, and she stopped. The rule can be fixed in Lab 2.

Lighting broke the rules. What will break end-to-end?
Днём на стол поставили горячий чайник —: In daylight, a hot kettle was put on the table, right between the hand and the cup.
<b>Версия end-to-end врезалась, остальны:
The end-to-end version crashed, the others went around. There was no kettle in the demonstrations. The network has no concept of "obstacle", only a learned habit of "going toward red". The planner in rules and in the hybrid goes around everything the detector marked as an obstacle (red cells), and that is a property of the algorithm, not statistics.

Can the network be taught to go around by showing demonstrations? Partly. But there is a catch: the operator goes around sometimes on the left, sometimes on the right, and a network trained on mean squared error averages "left" and "right" into "straight". We checked this on the same network: even with 1000 demonstrations of going around, it crashed almost every time. This is the problem of multimodal actions; lessons 1.3–1.5 are devoted to it.

Evening breaks the rules, the kettle breaks end-to-end. What happens when they come together?
Вечерний свет и чайник на пути одновреме: Evening light and a kettle in the way at the same time.
<b>Справился только гибрид.</b> Его нейр:
Only the hybrid made it. Its network is responsible for what and where: it finds the cup in any light. The rules are responsible for how: they build a path around the kettle and watch over safety. Most products of 2026 are built this way.

But the smart part here is the network: it is the one that tells the hybrid where the goal is. What happens when it sees something that was not in the data?
Дома появились новые бирюзовые чашки. Ни: New teal cups have appeared in the house. There were none in the rules or in the demonstrations.
<b>Не справился никто, но ошиблись они п:
Nobody made it, but they failed differently. The rules said "can't see the cup", and Ada stopped. This is a loud failure: you can call a human. End-to-end and the hybrid confidently drove to the bowl of coffee beans, the "reddest" blob in the frame, and stopped there as if the task were done. The network always gives an answer, even when it sees something that was not in the data. This is a silent failure: the system does not know it is wrong.

The hybrid does not help here. Rules guarantee its safety, but only data guarantees the right goal. Think about whose failure is more dangerous at home, with children and a cat around. We will return to this question in Part 8.

Понять просьбу: «принеси что-нибудь попи: Understand a request: "bring me something to drink, just not cold"
Язык бесконечно разнообразен: синонимы,: Language is infinitely varied: synonyms, slips, context. Keyword parsing breaks on the first unusual phrase; language models handle it. How policies understand language is Part 2.
Найти на столе свою кружку среди чужих: Find your own mug on the table among others
Восприятие в открытом мире — сильная сто: Open-world perception is a strength of neural networks. Mugs of every shape and color, in any light: rules cannot describe that, as Lab 1 showed.
Ткань деформируется непредсказуемо, план: Fabric deforms unpredictably, and a rules-based planner barely models it. That is how π0 learned to fold laundry: from thousands of hours of demonstrations.
Беспорядок бесконечно разнообразен. Типи: Mess is infinitely varied. A typical task for a learned policy.
Ручки, защёлки, направляющие — вариантов: Handles, latches, rails: thousands of variants. A policy trained on many drawers generalizes to a new one, while a rule would have to be written for each.
Налить воду в стакан и не пролить: Pour water into a glass without spilling
Жидкость трудно моделировать, а по демон: Liquid is hard to model, but from demonstrations a policy learns to pour smoothly. The water level can be controlled with a separate sensor, and then it is a hybrid.
Нейросеть замечает кошку в любой позе и: A neural network spots the cat in any pose and any light. But stopping in front of it is better set by a rule with a guarantee: "obstacle closer than 30 cm — stop".
Сбавить скорость, когда рядом ребёнок: Slow down when a child is nearby
Кто перед камерой, понимает нейросеть. С: Who is in front of the camera is understood by the network. How fast you may move near a person is set by a rule: it is a safety requirement, not statistics.
Управление усилием по датчику: замкнутый: Force control from a sensor: a closed loop at hundreds of hertz and clear physics. If a neural network hints how fragile the object is, that is already a hybrid.
Доехать до зарядки по известной карте: Drive to the charger on a known map
Квартира не меняется каждый день: карта,: The apartment does not change every day: a map, localization and a planner solve the task reliably and without data. Neural networks help here with unfamiliar obstacles.
Детерминированная логика и отдельная цеп: Deterministic logic and a separate power circuit. No place for probabilities here.
Помнить, что по вторникам поливаем цветы: Remember that we water the plants on Tuesdays
Ловушка: это не робототехника, а обычная: A trap: this is not robotics, just an ordinary program. Not everything in a robot needs to be learned.
<p><strong>Закономерность.</strong> Точн: The pattern. Precision, rate and safety stay with rules. Language, open-world perception, deformable objects and liquids go to neural networks. The experts gave ${counts.classic} of ${CARDS.length} tasks to rules, ${counts.nn} to end-to-end and ${counts.hybrid} to the hybrid. Where a guarantee is needed, rules stay, and the network takes what rules cannot describe. So how do real robots divide the work?
